title: The Spider-Man Bet

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: Okay, so movie theaters just bet their entire year on one Spider-Man movie?

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Basically, yeah. Brand New Day drops July thirty-first, and the tracking has it opening somewhere around a hundred-eighty to a hundred-ninety million. That's the biggest of the whole year.
lines.visual: range bar with Toy Story compare

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: I mean, that sounds great though, right? Why is that a bet?

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Here's the thing — AMC lost six hundred and thirty-two million dollars last year. And by their own math, every extra hundred million at the box office only adds about eighteen million to their bottom line.

viz.label: AMC NET LOSS — FY2025, SEC FILING

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: Oh wow. So they don't just want this to be big — they kind of need it to be huge.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Right. And the early signs are actually really good — the first-day presales are the best they've seen in five years. That puts it in Fandango's top ten of all time.

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: Okay, but I feel like there's a catch coming.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: There is. It's not getting a single IMAX screen opening weekend — Christopher Nolan's new movie locked up every one of them for a three-week run.

viz.resultLabel: BRAND NEW DAY  US IMAX SCREENS: 0
viz.caption: 3-WEEK EXCLUSIVE WINDOW

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: So even the experts must be all over the place on this one.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Completely split. Boxoffice Pro thinks it could hit two-thirty to two-fifty. For comparison, No Way Home did two hundred sixty — and only nine movies in history have ever opened above two hundred.
lines.visual: dual forecast vs No Way Home

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: And if it doesn't hit those numbers?

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Then it gets scary fast. AMC is sitting on four billion in debt with the stock under two bucks. So this really isn't just a movie premiere for them — it's the whole bet.

caption: Theater chains lost hundreds of millions last year. Now the whole quarter rides on one July 31 opening. Here's the math behind the Spider-Man bet.
